idiom_name: Vapor Leaf custom tag (LeafTag) registered in app.leaf.tags
implementation_notes: Server-side Swift presentation runs on Vapor with Leaf: a helper is a struct conforming to LeafTag whose render(_:) method receives a LeafContext (the call's parameters plus the view data) and returns LeafData, registered once with app.leaf.tags["name"] = MyTag(); templates then call #name(...). Formatting itself comes from Foundation (NumberFormatter, DateFormatter, FormatStyle) rather than from the tag, and a tag that must emit HTML has to conform to UnsafeUnescapedLeafTag and sanitise by hand. The tag struct is the helper - no class hierarchy is needed - and data retrieval stays in the route or controller that supplies the view data. Client-side SwiftUI reaches the same separation by construction (computed properties, ViewModifiers), so this file's materialization is the server-side one. A tag with stored configuration is justified when it is configured once at registration (locale, tenant); per-request values belong in the view data.
pitfalls: Leaf escapes tag output by default; conforming to UnsafeUnescapedLeafTag disables that, so any user-controlled value must be sanitised before it is returned.
NumberFormatter is neither Sendable nor thread-safe; a shared instance used across concurrent renders races - build one per render or prefer value-type formatting.
Tags are resolved by string name while rendering, so a typo or missing registration is a runtime failure, and returning empty LeafData renders nothing without raising.
Throwing from render(_:) aborts the page render; decide deliberately whether malformed input is an error or a fallback.
